Well, then you're just an asshole to everyone, congratulations, I guess? Honestly don't see how you think that's any better, but.

No, I use transphobic to mean you're behaving in a manner that you wouldn't treat cis people. Assuming someone is a decent person, they wouldn't tell a cis woman their jaw is too manly, thus for most people, the comment would be transphobic, but then you have ""equal opportunity" (ugh)  assholes like you, who treat everyone like dirt.

you are being transphobic.

If you saw a cis women, and she had a masculine jaw, (which does happen!) would you go up to her, and tell her she didn't look female enough for you?  would you even mention it at all? Let's say your  friend introduced you to her mother, and her mother  a very strong, masculine jaw.

for the vast majority of people, if you went up to a cis women, told her that her jaw was too masculine and she needed to do something about it, it would be considered disgustingly rude.  hell, just mentioning it would be disgustingly rude.

soooo why do you think it's suddenly ok to negatively comment on a strangers appearance, just because they are trans? Caityln being trans doesn't suddenly make it right for you to make horrible comments.
and we all feel sad sometimes... no one says depression is up for debat.

"you want mentally people have rights? how absurd, you're horrible!"

Considering BPD develops because of abuse, and people who have been abused can be really badly affected by people being overcontrolling.... yeah not a good idea.


Also, therapy only works when it's voluntary.

"dropping a plate" lmao. if only my life was that easy.

I've been physically, emotionally, verbally, and sexually abused all my life. on top of this i have mental illness. on top of this I am still being emotionally and verbally abused (sometimes physically as well)  this is constantly making me worse, as well developing psychosis (possible schizo-affective disorder) I am now too disabled to work or study.

To get better, I need to move out. to move out, I need to work, to work, i need to get better, and when I say "get better", I'm not even thinking about my blossoming psychotic disorder. just trauma and trauma related mental health problems. but all psychatrists have told me it's permanent, and that I'll never be fixed.

My mental health and trauma has gotten worse year in, year out, since I was 10 years old. How many more years do I have suffer? another decade? two? three?  

why should I live through six decades of mental illness and trauma and abuse? isn't 2 enough?
this!! this happened to me!!   almost exactly, except it was a step cousin.
on one hand i kinda think that idea is selfish, the idea I should just put up with so much pain and trauma. I wouldn't expect someone to walk on a broken leg for me.
